trans-unit.source: Open browser settings at the current local port. Settings also have a standalone launcher file.
Pause or resume system audio haptics.
Apply a listening profile while preserving whether audio haptics are paused.
Send one preset, including while audio haptics are paused.
A little closer to the music.
Pick a profile. Hear the difference, feel the change.
Selecting a profile updates the controls and saves immediately. Your audio source and paused state stay the same.
Start with sensitivity and spacing. More space gives each pulse room to land.
Choose how each pulse feels. Overall intensity is set in Logi Options+.
Test buttons send a single texture, even while paused. They do not change your settings.
Slow pulses during held bass notes. Leave off for a cleaner beat.
Keep a sound you like. Editing the live controls never overwrites a saved profile.
Save your current tuning, duplicate the selected original, or update an existing custom profile.
Recent bass and detail audio levels with detection thresholds
Playback follows your speakers or headphones. Input listens to a microphone, line-in, or virtual device.
Source changes require Use this source, so selecting a microphone does not start capturing it.
Haptic output is managed by Logi Options+. This selector only changes the audio being analyzed.
Timings are milliseconds since reload. They exclude physical vibration latency. Events sent counts API calls, not confirmed vibrations.
Audio stays on your computer. The plugin does not record or upload it. Changing profiles preserves your audio source and whether haptics are paused.
Higher detects quieter sounds. 50 keeps the base thresholds.
More space feels cleaner; less space follows faster rhythms.
Boost or reduce which bass attacks are picked up.
Reduce if vocals and bright instruments create too many taps.
100 Hz is a useful starting point for kicks and bass.
Focus on instrument attacks and upper-frequency detail.
Lower picks up smaller rises above sustained music.
Prevents a single attack being detected repeatedly in the same band.
How far an onset must rise above the slower background.
Must be lower than background contrast.
Must be longer than envelope attack and release.
Level above the effective bass floor that selects the stronger preset.
Avoids late playback when audio arrives in large buffers.
Minimum bass level for the optional texture. Sensitivity also applies.
Must be at least the loud-bass spacing.
The shared pulse spacing still applies.
Unavailable — reconnect or choose another source
Choose a source, then use it. Microphone capture starts only after you confirm the source.
You can still choose a default source or refresh again.
Use this source will start capturing the selected input.
Choose Use this source to switch playback capture.
Enable bass detection to use sustained texture.
Changes are not saved. Retry saving, or reload saved settings.
Reload saved settings if they changed elsewhere.
Wait for the current save to finish.
— use Reload saved settings to retry.
Choose a profile to apply its tuning immediately. You can undo the change.
Original profile duplicated. Select the copy to use it.
Another pulse is still using the playback slot. Try again.
Audio capture and analysis are paused. Turn on Audio haptics to resume. Preset previews remain available.
Settings applied. Waiting briefly for the detector to settle.
Play audio through the selected source.
No recent audio packets. Last sample
Audio is arriving. Feel for pulses around the attacks.
max. Last event age within its delivered batch:
. Diagnostic logs keep at most three 512 KiB files.
Plugin unavailable. Reopen the settings launcher or use Open haptic settings in Options+. The port changes after reload.
Capture restarted. Play audio through the selected source.
Balanced rhythm with rounded bass and quieter detail taps.
Bass attacks only, with extra low-band sensitivity.
Fewer, softer pulses for background listening.
Emphasizes deep bass attacks and reduces bright detail; sustained texture stays off.
More separation between impacts in dense mixes, with restrained upper-band taps.
Softer taps and wider spacing for lighter arrangements; detail remains enabled.
Sparse low-end impacts. Dialogue and soundtrack are not recognized separately.
Separated, higher-threshold impacts. Reacts to game audio; does not identify gameplay events.
Experimental slow soft pulses during held bass (280–650 ms spacing). Pulse rate follows energy, not tempo.
Reopen settings using the launcher or Open haptic settings action.
Settings changed elsewhere. Reload current settings before saving this draft.
Profiles changed elsewhere. Reload saved settings before saving a profile.
A profile with that name already exists. Choose another name.
Only an existing custom profile can be updated. Save a new copy instead.
Profile name must contain 1–64 characters without control characters.
Custom profiles could not be loaded. Saved data was preserved; restart the plugin after resolving the storage error.
Settings revision limit reached. Restart the plugin before saving more changes.
Profile revision limit reached. Saved profiles remain available, but further changes cannot be saved.
Could not load translations. Try again.
Custom profile. Apply to restore its saved tuning; paused state is preserved.
You can save up to 32 custom profiles.
The operation failed. Check capture status or the plugin log, then retry.
Sensitivity affects both bands. Pulse spacing limits how often markers can become haptic pulses.
Mint lines show bass: solid is the audio level, dashed is its adaptive threshold.
Purple lines show detail: solid is the audio level, dashed is its adaptive threshold.
Circles mark level-triggered pulses. Background contrast sets how far the dashed threshold sits above the background in both bands.
Diamonds mark sudden increases in audio level. Attack contrast sets the required rise within the rise window. These can happen below the dashed line.

Circle: level trigger. Diamond: rapid-rise trigger. Marker fill and number identify the sent texture; the outline matches the bass or detail line. Hollow markers have unknown texture. Markers show sent attacks, not confirmed vibrations.
Shape the envelopes and timing limits. Band and trigger controls are in Tune; related limits adjust together to stay valid.
Audio packets are arriving, but no signal is detected. Check playback routing and recording permission; silence alone does not prove permission was denied.
Audio signal detected. Feel for pulses around the attacks.
Starting audio capture. If macOS asks for permission, choose Allow. Installation can finish while you decide.
In macOS System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, enable Feel the Rhythm Capture, then retry capture.
In macOS System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording → System Audio Recording Only, enable Feel the Rhythm Capture, then retry capture.
For microphone access, enable access for desktop apps in Windows privacy settings, then retry capture.
The audio backend reported that access was denied.
If macOS asks to record audio, choose Allow. Capture will continue automatically after permission is granted.
Permission status is unknown. If audio is playing but the graph stays flat, check your audio source and recording permissions.
Check the system settings window, then return here and retry capture.
Preview recent entries or download the retained logs for a support report. Logs may contain device names and local paths; review them before sharing.
Logs load only when you request them. The preview shows up to 32,768 characters.
Log download prepared. Review the file before sharing.
Recent logs loaded. Download logs includes all retained files.
No log entries are available yet.
Request timed out. The change may already have completed. Reload saved settings before retrying.
Compare with the level this many milliseconds ago. Shorter favors sharp attacks; longer catches slower rises. No added waiting delay; rounded to about 5 ms frames.
Lower Q covers more frequencies; higher Q isolates a narrower band. Center gain is preserved.
Looks backward: shorter favors sharp attacks, longer catches slower rises. No extra waiting delay.
Minimum interval between detections in this band. Shared pulse spacing still applies.
Minimum relative positive spectral change. Lower detects smaller changes; applies only to spectral mode.
Square: spectral trigger. Dashed lines show envelope thresholds, not spectral thresholds.
Experimental frequency-change detection for detail, with envelope bass and no confirmation delay.
Spectral mode only. 0 is off; larger values tolerate wider pitch movement but may miss nearby new notes.
0 sends immediately. Otherwise wait this long and keep the strongest eligible peak. Adds real latency; event-age limit adjusts with it.
Limit how late a detected event may play. Detection controls are in the Detection tab.
Shared by envelope detectors using rapid rise. Each band has its own rise window above.
Shared envelope background and level-trigger settings. Spectral mode uses its own threshold.
Audio is currently silent. Signal was received earlier in this capture session.
